How the grid works

1
Each row is one beat. Music is counted in beats: 1, 2, 3, 4. The numbers on the left of the grid are the beats. Four beats make one bar, and most rhythms here are 2 bars long.
2
Each beat is split into 4 equal parts — the 4 squares in the row. You can count them out loud as "1 e & a" (one – ee – and – ah).
1e&a
3
Dark square = play. Grey square = rest (silence). The first square is always exactly on the beat.

Examples — tap ▶ to hear each one

All fourFour even hits in the beat: 1 e & a
On the beatOne hit, right on the count: 1
Beat and off-beatOn the beat and exactly halfway: 1 &
Off-beat onlySilent on the beat, hit halfway: &
Beat and last partOn the beat, then just before the next one: 1 … a

Tip: when you play an example, the blue outline shows where you are, and you'll hear a click on every beat.
